claims.original_source_locator: line 50, columns 863-870: All retained history before each origin, including earlier test history, is available to the candidate intensity. Each fit uses only its training prefix. The exponential mark-rate estimate is obtained from training marks alone and is common across candidate families; it is a plug-in estimate rather than a joint marked-intensity maximum-likelihood estimate. The reported score is the full marked-event score: the sum of event log intensities and log mark densities minus the integrated intensity over quiet exposure, with the final censor handled explicitly in the declared protocol. The uninhibited fit is retained as an exact eligible point in the inhibited search, so nonnegative training gain is partly built into candidate selection. This fact limits any inference from training improvement alone. The stored training gains for the shared diagnostic are \(2.731009\), \(0.302486\), and \(0.143866\), but those numbers are not treated as evidence of predictive success.

claims.original_source_locator: line 85, columns 55-57: All six selected Mittag--Leffler kernels use \(\alpha=0.5\), the lower searched grid endpoint, and \(\tau=1\) day, an interior grid value. The common selected productivity ratio is \(r=0.4\) at the first origin and \(r=0.7\) at the later origins; the former is the lower searched ratio endpoint. The Omori coordinates \(c,p\) were optimized continuously with a retained coarse-grid floor; they are not merely grid winners. This is a finite-window statement; no stationarity or burn-in argument is needed.

These are weights on a globally redistributed trigger component; they are not literal cross-zone offspring probabilities. Isotropy is Euclidean in the declared cylindrical equal-area projection, not geodesic equivalence. The appropriate scientific conclusion is a strong location-density improvement for this continuous triggering procedure, with no accompanying timing improvement and no meaningful incremental inhibition gain.

claims.source_locator: line 7, columns 206-208: A matched comparison of twelve earthquake forecasting models finds positive predictive evidence from continuous event locations and, within that representation, Omori temporal decay. The experiment reuses 612 historical targets across three chronological windows. A training-only kernel-density background reduces but does not remove the continuous-location advantage over a cell approximation: gains remain 2.326-2.369 nats per event across three temporal families. With that stronger background and continuous locations, Omori improves on fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler (ML) triggering by 15.474 joint-score nats, including 10.368 timing nats, with both components positive in every window. The fully combined procedure improves aggregate timing and location scores over its current matched coarse comparator; location prediction accounts for most of the gain. Negative temporal contrasts and losing 1-2 km sensitivity fits limit the interpretation. These are retrospective fitted-procedure comparisons, not independent confirmation, identification of physical triggering, or evidence for inhibition.

The experiment reuses 612 historical targets across three chronological windows. With that stronger background and continuous locations, Omori improves on fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler (ML) triggering by 15.474 joint-score nats, including 10.368 timing nats, with both components positive in every window. The fully combined procedure improves aggregate timing and location scores over its current matched coarse comparator; location prediction accounts for most of the gain. Negative temporal contrasts and losing 1-2 km sensitivity fits limit the interpretation. These are retrospective fitted-procedure comparisons, not independent confirmation, identification of physical triggering, or evidence for inhibition.

claims.source_locator: line 39, columns 37-39: Fixed ML uses the pinned normalized 195-mode mixture at one day. Common ML estimates its scale over 0.001-20 days; Omori estimates c over 0.0001-20 days and p over 1.01-2.5. Temporal kernels have unit mass over all positive lags, with exact finite-window exposure rather than window renormalization. Spatial scale sigma is selected once per fold by the fixed-ML/cell-background/continuous baseline from 5, 15, 50, 150, 500 and 1500 km, then shared across all twelve primary procedures. Free parameters are refitted separately within each procedure. These are conditional shared-scale comparisons, not independent spatial optimization for every model. The [frozen protocol](../research_results/temporal_spatial_background/protocol_observed_v1.json) specifies bounds, starts and selection rules.

semantic_binding.meaning: Abstract: The temporal and spatial forecast improvements in Addendum III survive some useful external comparisons, but their scope narrows when stronger benchmarks, conditional diagnostics a

source_refs.source_text: The frozen procedure transferred descriptively to the three California test windows: both primary score contrasts were positive in every window, with positive pooled differences. Across 315 held-out targets, Omori continuous improved timing over fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler continuous by 37.790339 nats, or 0.119969 nats per target. Omori continuous improved conditional location over Omori lifted by 674.323522 nats, or 2.140710 per target. All three contextual contrasts were also positive in all three windows. These are audited retrospective likelihood comparisons, with markedly uneven contributions across windows and score components. The [approved aggregate summary](../results/analysis/summary.json) preserves the complete values and components; its [release acceptance](../reviews/aggregate_release_conductor_acceptance_v1.json) authorizes reporting.
| O-C minus F-C: primary timing | Timing | +37.790339 | +0.119969 | 3/3 |
| O-C minus O-L: primary location | Conditional location | +674.323522 | +2.140710 | 3/3 |

All rows use 315 targets and all three complete windows. Totals are summed before dividing by target count, rather than averaging window means equally. Displayed scores are rounded to six decimal places; this is numerical reporting precision, not measurement accuracy. Joint differences for the two primary pairs are +38.969397 and +708.223703 nats respectively. The complete-procedure contrast has its own reference arm; it is not obtained by adding the two primary contrasts.

This JMA result reproduces the spatial direction but reverses the timing direction. OC loses 58.593466 timing nats to FC (-0.045884 nats per record), while gaining 1905.743202 conditional-location nats over OL (+1.492360 per record). Each direction holds in all three windows. The registered combined timing-and-location transfer criterion is therefore not demonstrated.

EP also beats OC on joint score in all three windows: OC–EP is -221.211492 nats (-0.173227 per record). The conditional-location component accounts for 213.485907 nats of that deficit. The continuous spatial procedures beat their respective cell-lift alternatives, including FC–FL under the fixed temporal kernel; this spatial result does not establish superiority over the stronger EP reference.
Combined descriptive transfer assessment: **not_demonstrated**.

The targets are the same three California windows used in prior work: 79, 167 and 69 events (315 total). Those outcomes were already inspected before this benchmark. The comparison is therefore exploratory and retrospective; it is not a new holdout or independent confirmation.

claims.original_source_locator: line 7, columns 328-335: The temporal and spatial forecast improvements in Addendum III survive some useful external comparisons, but their scope narrows when stronger benchmarks, conditional diagnostics and a third region are considered together. In California, Omori continuous (OC) improves timing over fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler continuous (FC) by 0.119969 nats per target and conditional location over Omori lifted (OL) by 2.140710, across 315 targets. OC also beats a separately refitted no-trigger procedure (N0), while a fitted inverse-power ETAS benchmark (EP) beats OC on joint score in every window, mainly through location. Conditional simulation of the original frozen OC forecast reveals material count, temporal and spatial discrepancies; it supplies no calibration result for EP. A higher-threshold sensitivity retains the primary directions, while annual and sequence accounting show marked concentration. Japan reproduces the continuous-versus-lifted location direction but reverses the Omori-versus-fixed-ML timing direction: its registered combined transfer criterion is not demonstrated. All archives had been inspected and revised; the comparisons are exploratory retrospective evidence, not pristine confirmation, physical causality or proof of forecast adequacy.

source_refs.source_text: A matched comparison of twelve earthquake forecasting models finds positive predictive evidence from continuous event locations and, within that representation, Omori temporal decay. The experiment reuses 612 historical targets across three chronological windows. A training-only kernel-density background reduces but does not remove the continuous-location advantage over a cell approximation: gains remain 2.326-2.369 nats per event across three temporal families. With that stronger background and continuous locations, Omori improves on fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler (ML) triggering by 15.474 joint-score nats, including 10.368 timing nats, with both components positive in every window. The fully combined procedure improves aggregate timing and location scores over its current matched coarse comparator; location prediction accounts for most of the gain. Negative temporal contrasts and losing 1-2 km sensitivity fits limit the interpretation. These are retrospective fitted-procedure comparisons, not independent confirmation, identification of physical triggering, or evidence for inhibition.

semantic_binding.meaning: 3.1 Population and chronological windows: The repaired California source contains 1,272 canonical unique preferred SCEDC/SCSN records meeting reported M >= 4.0, latitude 32-37 degrees, longitude -121 to -114 degrees and de

source_refs.source_text: The population uses preferred SCEDC/SCSN earthquakes with M>=4, latitude 32-37 degrees, longitude -121 to -114 degrees and depth -5 to 40 km. Its 1,272 unique events include 106 warmup parents from 1981-1985. Scored training starts in 1986 and expands to each origin, with 851, 930 and 1,097 targets. Strictly earlier test events may enter parent history under frozen rules; parameters and nuisance quantities do not update within a test window. Outside-domain and subthreshold parents are absent.

All rows use 315 targets and all three complete windows. Totals are summed before dividing by target count, rather than averaging window means equally. Displayed scores are rounded to six decimal places; this is numerical reporting precision, not measurement accuracy. Joint differences for the two primary pairs are +38.969397 and +708.223703 nats respectively. The complete-procedure contrast has its own reference arm; it is not obtained by adding the two primary contrasts.

The frozen procedure transferred descriptively to the three California test windows: both primary score contrasts were positive in every window, with positive pooled differences. Across 315 held-out targets, Omori continuous improved timing over fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler continuous by 37.790339 nats, or 0.119969 nats per target. Omori continuous improved conditional location over Omori lifted by 674.323522 nats, or 2.140710 per target. All three contextual contrasts were also positive in all three windows. These are audited retrospective likelihood comparisons, with markedly uneven contributions across windows and score components. The [approved aggregate summary](../results/analysis/summary.json) preserves the complete values and components; its [release acceptance](../reviews/aggregate_release_conductor_acceptance_v1.json) authorizes reporting.

source_refs.source_text: The original stop and its files remain sealed. In this explicitly authorized continuation, the parser accepts unused location-quality metadata as opaque printable tokens. All 45 cached official files were reused unchanged, with no query and no row editing, removal or imputation. All 134 previously rejected occurrences were retained: none was an M>=4 model candidate; five were M>=2 diagnostic candidate occurrences. Independent reconstruction verified exact equality of the old training model and diagnostic event arrays. The forecasting engine was unchanged. The [methods and repair section](methods_and_source_repair_v2.md) gives the source and control evidence.

source_refs.source_text: The timing advantage is almost absent in the first window. The middle window supplies about 87% of the pooled timing difference, so the positive signs do not imply a uniform effect. The timing contrast also has a negative conditional-location difference in 2016-2021 (-4.067620 nats), although its joint difference remains positive. Reporting components avoids treating every improvement as a general gain on every aspect of forecasting.

The frozen procedure transferred descriptively to the three California test windows: both primary score contrasts were positive in every window, with positive pooled differences. Across 315 held-out targets, Omori continuous improved timing over fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler continuous by 37.790339 nats, or 0.119969 nats per target. Omori continuous improved conditional location over Omori lifted by 674.323522 nats, or 2.140710 per target. All three contextual contrasts were also positive in all three windows. These are audited retrospective likelihood comparisons, with markedly uneven contributions across windows and score components. The [approved aggregate summary](../results/analysis/summary.json) preserves the complete values and components; its [release acceptance](../reviews/aggregate_release_conductor_acceptance_v1.json) authorizes reporting.

source_refs.source_text: Most of the primary location gain is within-cell density: +653.602228 of +674.323522 nats. The lifted offspring representation assigns uniform density within a cell, whereas the continuous representation resolves variation within it; the immigrant component remains smooth in both. The result therefore supports this particular spatial representation comparison. It does not show an equally large improvement in assigning probability among broad zones or cells, nor establish that individual earthquake locations are generally predictable.

Productivity exponent r=0.7 is fixed. Magnitude-rate beta, background bandwidth h and offspring scale sigma use training data only. Both scale grids were fixed at 5, 15, 50, 150, 500 and 1,500 km; all folds selected h=sigma=5 km, the lower endpoint. This does not establish a physically optimal 5 km scale or justify finer resolution. No test-based grid expansion occurred. Eight prescribed starts, failure-only Powell recovery and retained floors/near-optimal candidates implement the frozen optimization policy.

source_refs.source_text: The population uses preferred SCEDC/SCSN earthquakes with M>=4, latitude 32-37 degrees, longitude -121 to -114 degrees and depth -5 to 40 km. Its 1,272 unique events include 106 warmup parents from 1981-1985. Scored training starts in 1986 and expands to each origin, with 851, 930 and 1,097 targets. Strictly earlier test events may enter parent history under frozen rules; parameters and nuisance quantities do not update within a test window. Outside-domain and subthreshold parents are absent.

The target is the agreed revised **reported-record** population: agency J, natural subsidiary 1, determination K/k/A, allowed primary magnitude types J/D/V/d/v, reported M≥4.5, depth 0–60 km, and the fixed projected study region. Primary and secondary magnitudes are kept separate. This is not a homogeneous Mw or complete physical-earthquake catalogue.

The held-out windows contain 1,277 records in total. All three training samples exceed 180 records and every training latitude zone exceeds 30. No date, threshold, region or forecasting procedure was selected using fit outcomes.

All rows use 315 targets and all three complete windows. Totals are summed before dividing by target count, rather than averaging window means equally. Displayed scores are rounded to six decimal places; this is numerical reporting precision, not measurement accuracy. Joint differences for the two primary pairs are +38.969397 and +708.223703 nats respectively. The complete-procedure contrast has its own reference arm; it is not obtained by adding the two primary contrasts.

source_refs.source_text: The targets are the same three California windows used in prior work: 79, 167 and 69 events (315 total). Those outcomes were already inspected before this benchmark. The comparison is therefore exploratory and retrospective; it is not a new holdout or independent confirmation.

OC is the archived, sealed California Omori continuous fit and score procedure. It has no new fit or post-test selection. N0 fixes branching at zero and refits its own time-rate parameters a,d on each training window under its training joint likelihood, using the common training-selected smooth background. It is not the constant-Poisson numerical floor and is not OC with the trigger parameter set to zero after fitting. EP is a separately fitted continuous-space marked Omori ETAS adaptation with a pure inverse-power radial offspring kernel, normalized over the fixed California rectangle for each parent. Its parameters and the shared background are selected from training data only. EP does not multiply its offspring kernel by OC's reference background, and its spatial range is magnitude-independent.

source_refs.source_text: The targets are the same three California windows used in prior work: 79, 167 and 69 events (315 total). Those outcomes were already inspected before this benchmark. The comparison is therefore exploratory and retrospective; it is not a new holdout or independent confirmation.

The held-out windows contain 1,277 records in total. All three training samples exceed 180 records and every training latitude zone exceeds 30. No date, threshold, region or forecasting procedure was selected using fit outcomes.

All arms retain the fixed productivity exponent r=0.7 and common training-only magnitude-rate beta. Their common marginal magnitude-mark log score is included once and cancels exactly in every contrast. The same target admission, strict earlier-parent rule, exposure and score measure apply. The OC−N0 comparison measures score differences between complete procedures with a shared trained geography; it is not a causal triggering test. OC−EP compares complete procedures with different offspring spatial laws and is not an isolated test of temporal kernel choice.

source_refs.source_text: The active indicator is defined by any admitted M≥6 anchor at u with u<t≤u+30 days, including eligible prehistory. Integer UTC membership, strict-past ties and global merging precede fold clipping. The initial anchor is in the complement unless an earlier anchor already activates its timestamp. One of the two test anchor targets is active and one is in the complement. Anchor event-only subset diagnostics remain private and independently audited; only their counts are released. **Interpretation and programme boundary.** Annual results, including 2019, were already inspected before the finer partition was chosen. This is a retrospective exploratory accounting exercise, not a new holdout, independent sequence replication, significance test, event-iid uncertainty calculation or calibration result. Relative proper-score differences do not establish absolute forecast adequacy. The prior [competitive benchmark](../../competitive_benchmarks_20261025T065609Z/reports/decision_report.md) still favors EP overall, and prior [conditional diagnostics](../../conditional_calibration_20261025T085151Z/reports/decision_report.md) found material OC count, timing and spatial discrepancies. This audit resolves where the specified realised gains occur; it does not resolve those calibration limitations or establish physical causation.

source_refs.source_text: For calendar 2019, the active period contributes +30.058155064 timing nats against fixedML, +375.944700694 location nats against OL, and +9.878145249 joint nats against commonML. The six-target 2019 complement contributes -0.777558252, +16.828728374 and -1.898745079 nats respectively. Thus the positive 2019 timing and commonML joint totals arise in the active period, with negative complement contributions; most of the 2019 location gain also occurs there. Across all fifteen test years, each contextual primary difference remains positive in the complement: +7.732184195 timing, +298.378821253 location and +11.299739148 joint nats. Concentration in 2019 does not mean that every pooled contextual gain is confined to that episode.

**Three contextual comparisons.** Each column has its own reference and primary component; the columns must never be added. Parentheses divide that row's summed nats by that row's target count. Pooled means use the summed original-fold scores divided by 315, 110 or 205 as appropriate; they do not average fold means. All sixteen reporting rows per contrast are retained, including the sole episode and both empty active rows.

source_refs.source_text: Fitting completed in 544.5848309 seconds; the [separate independent saved-output audit](../reviews/full_saved_audit_independent_acceptance_v1.json) completed in 1892.9961546 seconds, as recorded by its [process receipt](independent-full-saved-audit-v1_process.json). All 30 procedures, 240 starts and 33 floors were accounted for, and all 15 fold/model statuses were complete. Independent auditing, rather than solver completion alone, supports release of these comparisons.

The independent raw-history audit passed for all three windows and all six new fit procedures. It reconstructed 57 candidates, 48 finite solver returns, 57 candidate forecasts, 48 solver-return forecasts and three sealed OC replays. All 22 audited bindings matched. The maximum absolute reconstruction error was 8.185452315956354e−11 nat, below the 1e−4-nat gate. The maximum near-optimal forecast spread was 1.7979773279810747e−05 nat/target, strictly below the 0.01 gate. No window is unknown in the accepted aggregate.

The campaign comprised six new fit procedures, 48 prescribed starts and nine floors. The main fit phase took 101.66045 seconds; the score-only recovery phase took 85.75795 seconds; the independent raw audit took 557.32265 seconds. These are separate phase durations, not a speedup claim. The final controller-ledger v2 sums 23 serialized receipts to 1384.5658555 seconds (about 23.08 minutes), covering builds, failed controls, both resource-pilot epochs, fitting, both score attempts, audit, aggregate export and figures. That receipt sum excludes provider/native latency and isolated data-free tests, and is not CPU time or monetary cost.

The catalogue inventory admitted one prospectively specified M>=4.5 complete-procedure sensitivity. It rebuilt training estimates, eligible histories, mark law and fitted procedures for this observation law. The 391-event population includes 33 warmup parents; training counts are 271, 287 and 340, and held-out counts are 16, 53 and 18 (87 total). All 30 procedures, 240 prescribed starts, 33 exact floors and 273 candidate slots completed. All 240 finite solver returns were audited; the accepted first-fold pilot was reused. The independent raw-row audit reconciled scores within 1.13e-11 nats. The additional annual reconstruction reconciled all 60 arm blocks and 45 contrast blocks within 1.14e-13 nats, retaining years with zero targets.

**Evidence and numerical scope.** All fifteen planned states completed; failed and missing states are zero. Independent raw-row reconstruction and saved-output comparison cover eighty arm rows and sixty-four contrast rows. All 7,128 component checks passed; maximum absolute discrepancy was 4.547473508864641e-13 nats against the 1e-4-nat gate. Production and independent scientific controls passed 161 and 101 checks, the exporter passed twelve controls, and eleven projection controls preceded 3,888 actual private-to-public projection checks with zero error and maximum difference zero. The projection retained every approved row while omitting anchor event-only scores, raw vectors, timestamps, membership hashes, source/event/fit IDs and fitted parameters.

The targets are the same three California windows used in prior work: 79, 167 and 69 events (315 total). Those outcomes were already inspected before this benchmark. The comparison is therefore exploratory and retrospective; it is not a new holdout or independent confirmation.

claims.source_locator: line 7, columns 175-177: The registered continuous local-inhibition (LI) procedure selects exactly zero inhibition strength in all three previously inspected California test windows. Across the same 315 targets used in the preceding comparisons, LI is a numerical tie with matched Omori continuous (OC); its raw pooled positive difference is only 1.884928e-10 total nats and is not a predictive gain. The inverse-power ETAS benchmark (EP) remains better jointly in every window, mainly through conditional location. All eight fixed-seed controls are retained: LI loses to OC on both uniform-null, both smooth-null and both narrow/short-inhibition datasets, and wins on both broad/long-inhibition datasets. Two seeds per regime cannot estimate power or a false-positive rate, and the narrow/short losses prevent a claim that this procedure would reliably detect inhibition when present. At zero inhibition, range and memory are unidentified. These results concern a frozen statistical extension that attenuates only the immigrant component at recorded coordinates; they do not establish absence of physical inhibition, causal mechanisms, significance or global optimization.

semantic_binding.meaning: Abstract: The registered continuous local-inhibition (LI) procedure selects exactly zero inhibition strength in all three previously inspected California test windows. Across the same 315 ta

source_refs.source_text: The registered LI procedure was a **numerical tie with OC in all three observed windows**, and all three selected LI fits had **Î· exactly zero**. No active inhibition term was selected. Relative to the sealed EP comparator, LI scored lower in every window: the event-weighted joint difference was **-0.162067316707528 nats per event**, or **-51.0512047628713 total nats** across 315 targets. This run therefore provides no predictive improvement over OC from the registered LI procedure and favors EP over LI on these observed joint scores.

The raw pooled LI-minus-OC difference is 1.88492776942439e-10 total nats (5.98389768071236e-13 per event). That tiny floating-point sign is a numerical tie, not evidence of improvement. Each window is within the prespecified 0.0002-total-nat descriptive tie threshold; the raw values remain available in the approved aggregate. This threshold is numerical, not a statistical significance test.

LI scored below OC on both uniform-null datasets, both smooth-null datasets and both narrow/short-inhibition datasets. It scored above OC on both broad/long-inhibition datasets. All eight prescribed datasets are shown separately; no seed or case was discarded or redrawn.

These eight fixed examples, with two seeds per regime, do not estimate a false-positive rate, statistical power or parameter-coverage probability. The contrast pattern describes this registered fitting procedure; it does not prove the absence of inhibition in the generating law or certify a globally optimal fit.

At η=0 the inhibition scales ℓ and ψ are unidentified. Their canonical displayed values are not recovered physical scales. The observed tie with OC and exact-zero η selections give no selected active-inhibition explanation for the observed forecasts. This does not establish that physical inhibition is absent from earthquakes. Even a positive fitted η would diagnose a term in this model, rather than establish a causal mechanism, statistical significance or physical scale recovery.

The evidence is limited to three observed windows and eight fixed synthetic datasets under the frozen recorded-coordinate observation law. There are no event-iid confidence intervals, Wilks-based tests, causal conclusions, physical-range conclusions or proof of absolute forecast calibration. Additional validation would be needed for broader generalization.

The fixed source contains 1,272 unique events: 106 warmup parents in 1981-1985 and 1,166 evaluated records in 1986-2026. semantic_binding.meaning: 2.1 Same California history, not a new sample: The observation law selects preferred California records with reported M >= 4.0, latitude 32-37 degrees, longitude -121 to -114 degrees and depth -5 to 40 km. The fixed source cont

source_refs.source_text: The population uses preferred SCEDC/SCSN earthquakes with M>=4, latitude 32-37 degrees, longitude -121 to -114 degrees and depth -5 to 40 km. Its 1,272 unique events include 106 warmup parents from 1981-1985. Scored training starts in 1986 and expands to each origin, with 851, 930 and 1,097 targets. Strictly earlier test events may enter parent history under frozen rules; parameters and nuisance quantities do not update within a test window. Outside-domain and subthreshold parents are absent.

All rows use 315 targets and all three complete windows. Totals are summed before dividing by target count, rather than averaging window means equally. Displayed scores are rounded to six decimal places; this is numerical reporting precision, not measurement accuracy. Joint differences for the two primary pairs are +38.969397 and +708.223703 nats respectively. The complete-procedure contrast has its own reference arm; it is not obtained by adding the two primary contrasts.

The frozen procedure transferred descriptively to the three California test windows: both primary score contrasts were positive in every window, with positive pooled differences. Across 315 held-out targets, Omori continuous improved timing over fixed-scale Mittag-Leffler continuous by 37.790339 nats, or 0.119969 nats per target. Omori continuous improved conditional location over Omori lifted by 674.323522 nats, or 2.140710 per target. All three contextual contrasts were also positive in all three windows. These are audited retrospective likelihood comparisons, with markedly uneven contributions across windows and score components. The [approved aggregate summary](../results/analysis/summary.json) preserves the complete values and components; its [release acceptance](../reviews/aggregate_release_conductor_acceptance_v1.json) authorizes reporting.

source_refs.source_text: The registered LI procedure was a **numerical tie with OC in all three observed windows**, and all three selected LI fits had **Î· exactly zero**. No active inhibition term was selected. Relative to the sealed EP comparator, LI scored lower in every window: the event-weighted joint difference was **-0.162067316707528 nats per event**, or **-51.0512047628713 total nats** across 315 targets. This run therefore provides no predictive improvement over OC from the registered LI procedure and favors EP over LI on these observed joint scores.

The raw pooled LI-minus-OC difference is 1.88492776942439e-10 total nats (5.98389768071236e-13 per event). That tiny floating-point sign is a numerical tie, not evidence of improvement. Each window is within the prespecified 0.0002-total-nat descriptive tie threshold; the raw values remain available in the approved aggregate. This threshold is numerical, not a statistical significance test.

LI scored below OC on both uniform-null datasets, both smooth-null datasets and both narrow/short-inhibition datasets. It scored above OC on both broad/long-inhibition datasets. All eight prescribed datasets are shown separately; no seed or case was discarded or redrawn.

These eight fixed examples, with two seeds per regime, do not estimate a false-positive rate, statistical power or parameter-coverage probability. The contrast pattern describes this registered fitting procedure; it does not prove the absence of inhibition in the generating law or certify a globally optimal fit.

At η=0 the inhibition scales ℓ and ψ are unidentified. Their canonical displayed values are not recovered physical scales. The observed tie with OC and exact-zero η selections give no selected active-inhibition explanation for the observed forecasts. This does not establish that physical inhibition is absent from earthquakes. Even a positive fitted η would diagnose a term in this model, rather than establish a causal mechanism, statistical significance or physical scale recovery.

The evidence is limited to three observed windows and eight fixed synthetic datasets under the frozen recorded-coordinate observation law. There are no event-iid confidence intervals, Wilks-based tests, causal conclusions, physical-range conclusions or proof of absolute forecast calibration. Additional validation would be needed for broader generalization.

source_refs.source_text: The registered LI procedure was a **numerical tie with OC in all three observed windows**, and all three selected LI fits had **Î· exactly zero**. No active inhibition term was selected. Relative to the sealed EP comparator, LI scored lower in every window: the event-weighted joint difference was **-0.162067316707528 nats per event**, or **-51.0512047628713 total nats** across 315 targets. This run therefore provides no predictive improvement over OC from the registered LI procedure and favors EP over LI on these observed joint scores.

The raw pooled LI-minus-OC difference is 1.88492776942439e-10 total nats (5.98389768071236e-13 per event). That tiny floating-point sign is a numerical tie, not evidence of improvement. Each window is within the prespecified 0.0002-total-nat descriptive tie threshold; the raw values remain available in the approved aggregate. This threshold is numerical, not a statistical significance test.

LI scored below OC on both uniform-null datasets, both smooth-null datasets and both narrow/short-inhibition datasets. It scored above OC on both broad/long-inhibition datasets. All eight prescribed datasets are shown separately; no seed or case was discarded or redrawn.

These eight fixed examples, with two seeds per regime, do not estimate a false-positive rate, statistical power or parameter-coverage probability. The contrast pattern describes this registered fitting procedure; it does not prove the absence of inhibition in the generating law or certify a globally optimal fit.

At η=0 the inhibition scales ℓ and ψ are unidentified. Their canonical displayed values are not recovered physical scales. The observed tie with OC and exact-zero η selections give no selected active-inhibition explanation for the observed forecasts. This does not establish that physical inhibition is absent from earthquakes. Even a positive fitted η would diagnose a term in this model, rather than establish a causal mechanism, statistical significance or physical scale recovery.

The evidence is limited to three observed windows and eight fixed synthetic datasets under the frozen recorded-coordinate observation law. There are no event-iid confidence intervals, Wilks-based tests, causal conclusions, physical-range conclusions or proof of absolute forecast calibration. Additional validation would be needed for broader generalization.

source_refs.source_text: The registered LI procedure was a **numerical tie with OC in all three observed windows**, and all three selected LI fits had **Î· exactly zero**. No active inhibition term was selected. Relative to the sealed EP comparator, LI scored lower in every window: the event-weighted joint difference was **-0.162067316707528 nats per event**, or **-51.0512047628713 total nats** across 315 targets. This run therefore provides no predictive improvement over OC from the registered LI procedure and favors EP over LI on these observed joint scores.

The raw pooled LI-minus-OC difference is 1.88492776942439e-10 total nats (5.98389768071236e-13 per event). That tiny floating-point sign is a numerical tie, not evidence of improvement. Each window is within the prespecified 0.0002-total-nat descriptive tie threshold; the raw values remain available in the approved aggregate. This threshold is numerical, not a statistical significance test.

LI scored below OC on both uniform-null datasets, both smooth-null datasets and both narrow/short-inhibition datasets. It scored above OC on both broad/long-inhibition datasets. All eight prescribed datasets are shown separately; no seed or case was discarded or redrawn.

The contrast pattern describes this registered fitting procedure; it does not prove the absence of inhibition in the generating law or certify a globally optimal fit.

The observed tie with OC and exact-zero η selections give no selected active-inhibition explanation for the observed forecasts. This does not establish that physical inhibition is absent from earthquakes. Even a positive fitted η would diagnose a term in this model, rather than establish a causal mechanism, statistical significance or physical scale recovery.

The evidence is limited to three observed windows and eight fixed synthetic datasets under the frozen recorded-coordinate observation law. There are no event-iid confidence intervals, Wilks-based tests, causal conclusions, physical-range conclusions or proof of absolute forecast calibration. claims.source_locator: line 73, columns 254-256: The historical controlled studies have a different role. They compare declared laws and procedures, using saved simulated histories and retained failure/recovery policies. When generating nuisance parameters are supplied, the known-law test detects all 150 saved alternatives and rejects 50 of 1,000 separate null queries. Estimating inhibition alone with those nuisance values supplied also detects all 150 alternatives. Estimating background level with trend supplied detects 123, whereas estimating level and trend detects 68. The earlier fuller fitted procedure detects 57 after its own recalibration. These contrasts are substantive evidence about these procedures, with conditional uncertainty and adaptive-reuse qualifications. They are not five independent replications, an additive causal decomposition, or a proof that fixing unknown background values is appropriate for the observed analysis. A subsequent four-procedure continuation is distinguished in Section~\ref{sec:f-continuation} and the accompanying F addendum; its new numerical contract and incomplete null coverage do not replace these historical results.
